Maths Path · Ages 9 to 10

Class 5 maths

Decimals, angles, averages and logic. Go in order. Pass each check to open the next chapter.

0 of 10 passed

Class 5 chapters in order

  1. 1

    Large numbers and place-value clues

    Read seven- and eight-digit values and justify comparison or rounding.

    • I can build and compare large numbers.
    • I can round and solve digit clues.
    • I can use Roman numerals.
    Not started
  2. 2

    Solve stories with factors and multiples

    Choose a method, use exact groups or repeating schedules, and check the result.

    • I can solve a linked calculation story.
    • I can find common factors and multiples.
    • I can use a repeating schedule and interpret leftovers.
    Not started
  3. 3

    Fractions, mixed numbers and what is left

    Connect pictures and quantities before solving repeated changes.

    • I can match equivalent and mixed fractions.
    • I can order fractions and find a fraction of an amount.
    • I can find what is left after fraction changes.
    Not started
  4. 4

    Tenths, hundredths and decimal calculations

    Connect fractions and place value, then line up decimal places.

    • I can show decimals on a grid or line.
    • I can compare decimals and link them to fractions.
    • I can calculate decimal money and measures.
    Not started
  5. 5

    Angles, symmetry, perimeter and area

    Name the measurement needed before using shape facts.

    • I can find a perimeter or area.
    • I can use angle facts.
    • I can complete symmetry or fold a cube net.
    Not started
  6. 6

    Convert and compare measurements

    Read scales and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.

    • I can read a dial or thermometer.
    • I can compare mixed units.
    • I can solve a measurement story and estimate sensibly.
    Not started
  7. 7

    Elapsed time, timetables and dates

    Separate actual time, displayed time and calendar intervals.

    • I can find elapsed time.
    • I can correct clock errors and switch time formats.
    • I can use a calendar and timetable.
    Not started
  8. 8

    Plan a budget and compare value

    Compare like quantities and account for every price change.

    • I can total purchases and find missing prices.
    • I can compare value for money.
    • I can check a budget after a discount.
    Not started
  9. 9

    Charts, averages and true statements

    Read the scale, combine results and justify a claim.

    • I can read pictographs and scaled bars.
    • I can compare two displays or a line graph.
    • I can find an average and check a chart statement.
    Not started
  10. 10

    Codes, reflections and logic puzzles

    Test every clue and distinguish turning, mirroring and flipping.

    • I can use codes, series and ranking clues.
    • I can follow directions and count combinations.
    • I can reason about mirror clocks and reflected words.
    • I can order words by their logical meaning and find an exact embedded figure.
    Not started

Olympiad-style paper

When the chapters feel easy, try a mixed paper written in the style of Olympiad papers. The questions are original to Otterly, and this is not an official exam.
